correctness.rationale: The 28-pair Plotkin count excludes n>=8 and the three-coordinate injectivity bound caps code size at 8. XOR normalization gives a bijection from arbitrary optimal codes containing zero to seven-cliques of the entire pair-metric candidate graph. Every clique is searched by a complete ascending-depth recursion for each n=3..7; all counted codes are XOR-closed and the counts are 1,1,5,4,2 through zero. Independent all-linear-subspace enumeration reproduces these counts and independent 5^7 grouped enumeration reproduces the length-seven count. The coset count is 2^(n-3). All three supplied standalone programs executed successfully from their actual paths.

value.rationale: A natural complete endpoint classification, not a single arbitrary finite table: for a binary read-two-symbol channel with three information bits and pair distance n-1, the Singleton and Plotkin inequalities restrict the entire possible length range to 3..7. The result rules out all nonlinear alternative optimum designs across this range and supplies exact labeled multiplicities 1,2,20,32,32. This specifically answers whether extra design freedom from nonlinear codes changes the equality-case landscape. Linear examples and class uniqueness do not supply that answer. The n=6 subcase was previously obtained and is not counted as a separate new contribution.
